P1.evidence: The frame is two parts of four: 'I just want to understand, like, where are you at? Like, what's going on? Where are you at right now with your fitness, nutrition, everything? And where are you trying [to go]' — where you are and where you want to go, but nothing on what's in the way or what you need. No agreement question was asked, so P1c is a miss. P1d is present in the same breath and the prospect answers it at length. P1a is a miss rather than N/A: a setter did pre-qualify him the day before ('I can tell you also everything what I tell to your colleague yesterday') and the rep never read anything back.

P2.evidence: Strong on the lifestyle facts, weak on the medical ones. Age and height were asked directly ('How old are you? Because I didn't get that', 'how tall are you'). Work was asked twice, including the desk-versus-feet question: 'on a daily basis, what's your workday? Do you sit a lot or do you move?' Training week and diet were covered in depth. P2c is a straight miss — health conditions and hereditary history were never raised at all with a 50-year-old. P2d is partial: the rep only followed up injuries the prospect had already volunteered ('apart from this ankle injury that you mentioned and something on your hand?') and never asked an open limitations question or how long anything had lasted. P2f is partial because the 112 kg to 96 kg result was volunteered, not asked for. P2h is partial — sleep was asked inside a compound question, 'how about your recovery? in terms of how's your sleep, energy levels during the day?', and the prospect answered only on energy; the rep never came back to sleep.

P3.evidence: The bridge question ran cleanly — 'in your mind, like what's the biggest reason why you want to actually do this?' — and so did a value question, 'like what would that moment be worth to you?' But the answer came back at the same surface level it started ('The biggest reason is what I told you, sport') and the rep accepted it. P3f and P3g are the defining misses of this call: the prospect has a wife, a large business and turns 51 in August, and not one question touched family, legacy, longevity or identity. P3c was never asked. P3h is partial — 'in your case, it's not really about surviving, it's just becoming like top level, the next level' is a reflect-back, but it reflects the surface goal rather than anything deeper, because nothing deeper was ever surfaced.

P4.evidence: P4a and P4b ran: 'we had trainers in the past, like personal trainers, right?' followed by what came of it ('I was at that time in amazing shape'). P4e is the best moment in the phase — the rep asked 'why not to double down on that?' and the prospect named the gap himself: 'When you have obligation with somebody and have respect with the other person, you must understand. So that's the biggest benefit with personal trainer.' P4c is partial because the rep took the first, logistical answer (the trainers became unavailable) and did not press on why it stopped working. P4f never ran, which matters here — this prospect is unusually self-directed and 'why can't you stick to it on your own' was the obvious question.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was skipped in full. There is no two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The rep moved directly from the podium value question at 00:21:35 into 'Okay, Sasa, I feel very confident about actually how can we help you' and started the pillar pitch at 00:25:21. Nothing in this call makes the cost of inaction real, which is the likeliest reason a prospect with no price objection still would not pay at the end.

P6.evidence: Both questions were asked in substance. P6a: 'if you had this right training, the simple nutrition, and the real accountability from Trevor built around your specific schedule and life, would you agree that you would actually get to that goal of getting stronger and possibly getting the first place?' P6b: 'if we figure out the details are you fully committed to to showing up and doing the work to become 100%'. P6c is the failure. The answer to P6a was hedged — 'I think it's possible. I think, yes, I will go' — which is exactly the 'could' language his manager had drilled him on the previous day, and the rep did not press for certainty. He then undercut his own P6b by dismissing it aloud twice: 'I don't think I need to ask that but...' and 'yeah I know I didn't have to ask that but still'. He proceeded to price on a soft yes.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted so the phase applies. P11a is partial: the link was sent ('I will put in the chat the payment link') but no payment was collected and the prospect ultimately declined to use it. P11b is partial: the Trevor call was described and promised ('When we go through the payment, I book you a call with Trevor right away') but never actually scheduled. P11c and P11d never happened — no agreement email, no signature on the call, no welcome email, no Skool link, no onboarding questionnaire. The rep also filled the silence after sending the link with unrelated small talk about windsurfing, which is precisely the technique his manager coached the day before, and it did not hold: the prospect used the gap to ask for an app demo.

objection_plays.detail: SCRIPT GAP — no play exists for 'show me the product before I pay.' This was the only objection in the call and it killed the close. The prospect asked four times in escalating specificity: a demo, then a video, then any screenshots, then finally just an empty app menu ('You have this empty app, only send me a screenshot, I don't need app to install it on my phone'). The rep had no asset, no anonymised demo, and no scripted response. He improvised three reframes in sequence — the app is only a tool, look at Trevor's results, the app is the least of your problems — none of which address a due-diligence request, and then conceded the action. Worth noting that the confidentiality reason he gave ('we cannot share the client's details') is contradicted by his own conduct later the same day, when he screen-shared a named existing client's programme to the same prospect.
No money objection of any kind arose. The prospect restated the prices himself without resistance: 'especially if I'm paying $6,000 or $9,000, it doesn't matter.'
No think-it-over. The prospect chose a tier within seconds of hearing the price and said 'Ready to roll?' — 'Yes'.

notes: This is a well-qualified, pre-sold, price-insensitive buyer who did not pay, and the two causes are both process. First, the rep skipped Phase 5 completely — there is no cost of inaction anywhere in 43 minutes, so when a reason to delay appeared there was nothing pulling against it. Second, he accepted 'I think it's possible' as the commitment yes and then apologised for asking, so he went to price without a firm one. The coachable habit is the same one his manager named in the 1-1 the previous day: when resistance came he went straight to logistics and reframes instead of finding out what the resistance actually was. The separate, non-rep issue is an asset gap — the company has no shareable view of the app, and that alone is what the prospect stalled on.
